provenance.paper_title: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic GUI Agents via State Machine Memory

evidence.paraphrase: Crawler-validated GUI states and action templates form a state machine used to synthesize executable programs.

evidence.section: Full paper: Dynamic Memory Update Mechanism
evidence.paraphrase: Execution failures trigger fixed vision-based re-grounding and persistent memory updates. For ActionEngine, this specifically supports fixed-rule insertion or replacement of updatable GUI state-machine memory.
Failed actions are repaired and their state-machine entries corrected. For ActionEngine, this specifically supports fixed-rule correction of stored state of updatable GUI state-machine memory.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 8): During inference, the operative memory component (updatable GUI state-machine memory) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, fixed-rule correction of stored state; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
